messages:
Ariel Gomez: Heads-upCrestline Finance asked for a 10-day POC to validate a compatibility proxy that maps their incumbent vendor API to Redwood. Their priorities: token-for-token billing parity, faithful stop-token semantics, and completed security questionnaire. Can eng + security scope this?

Keisha Brown: I'll lead the technical POC. Immediate asks: (1) canonical prompt set (40), (2) a smaller 'known-failures' set (15), (3) explicit billing examples where tokens must match exactly. Also need their staging allowlist CIDR and desired latency SLO (they asked p95 < 220ms).

Liam O'Rourke: Re: token parity 1 practical approaches: run their tokenizer inside the adapter (accurate, added CPU), or pre-normalize inputs to reduce tokenization differences (cheaper, may not be exact). If they insist on exact invoice lines we have to run their tokenizer. For the POC we can do a small sidecar that pulls the vendor tokenizer binary.

Zara Khan: Security: they attached a 12-page secQ. Key items: no plaintext storage of customer API tokens, KMS integration (customer-managed preferred), SOC2 Type II evidence, pen-test summary, and regional data residency (EU). I'll own the secQ answers; please drop any ops/runbook artifacts here.

Keisha Brown: Example shim curl to hand to their infra showing mapping and header passthrough:

```bash
curl -X POST https://shim.crestline.poc/api/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <CREST_POC_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Crest-Request-Id: 4321" \
  -d '{"prompt":"Summarize invoice #304","max_tokens":64,"stop":["\\n\\n","END"],"temperature":0.0}'
```

Keisha Brown: Shim behaviour summary: map max_tokens->max_new_tokens, run vendor tokenizer to emit vendor_token_count in response metadata, echo passthrough headers (configurable list), and implement prioritized first-match stop semantics. We'll include a token-report header: X-Token-Report: vendor=123;redwood=123;delta=0.

Liam O'Rourke: Ops note: running vendor tokenizer in the adapter will increase CPU and may add ~20-40ms median latency; factor that into SLOs. For the POC we can spin up a small dedicated pool to isolate noise. Also need their allowlist IPs and an S3 bucket for exporting reconciliation logs (7-day retention).

Ariel Gomez: Commercial ask from the customer: prefer a fixed POC fee + usage but insisted billing must reconcile token-for-token with their invoicing. Keisha/Tess please propose 2 options (hosted shim with adapter surcharge, or Dedicated reserved pool).

Zara Khan: On KMS: for hosted POC we can support envelope encryption using our KMS and not store raw customer tokens. If they require BYOK/HSM for the POC mention Private deployment; we can do an HSM-backed demo but that is out-of-scope for a 10-day quick POC without commercial adjustments. I'll note that in secQ draft.

Keisha Brown: Acceptance criteria draft:
- median latency <= 140ms (single-turn short prompts), p95 <= 220ms in staging
- token_delta_rate <= 0.5% on canonical set (ideally 0%)
- no persisted plaintext customer API tokens
- parity diffs: provide CSV with columns: prompt_id, vendor_text, redwood_text, vendor_tokens, redwood_tokens, delta, sim_score

Liam O'Rourke: For similarity we will compute embedding cosine similarity + a lexical metric and flag sim_score < 0.83 for manual review. We'll also provide a small script to reproduce comparisons locally.

Ariel Gomez: Timeline they proposed: sandboxes up in 48h, run canonical & failure sets across days 3-8, tuning days 9-10, sign-off day 11. Can we shorten? They want quick results.

Keisha Brown: We can hit sandbox in 48-72 hours. Proposed cadence:
- Day 0-2: provision sandbox, allowlist, upload prompts
- Day 3-7: run canonical suite, produce diffs
- Day 8-9: remediate stop-token and tokenizer edge cases
- Day 10: final runs and acceptance artifacts

Zara Khan: I'll start the secQ answers. Please attach SOC2 summary, pen-test date, and any architecture diagrams showing token flow. Also confirm whether they need logs exported to their EU bucket (we can pin region).

Liam O'Rourke: Ops deliverable: runbook with allowlist steps, IAM role sample for cross-account S3 writes, and recommended dedicated pool configuration. I'll post the runbook link tomorrow.

Ariel Gomez: Action items: Keisha to deliver shim example + test harness repo; Liam to post ops runbook and dedicated pool spec; Zara to draft secQ responses & SOC2/pen-test snippets; Sales Ops to propose POC pricing options. Target: sandbox ready in 48-72 hours.

security-bot: Sandbox 'crestline-poc-11' provisioned (sbx-223). Vault: credentials uploaded, access granted to thread participants.

Keisha Brown: Starting harness now. Will post a repo and a sample token_report header format. Also adding a deterministic mode (seed + temp=0) for billing verification runs.

Ariel Gomez: Great. I'll schedule kickoff with Crestline for Thursday @ 09:30 CET. Thanks all. :pray:
